And we also saw during the presentation the importance of the payment sheets for clients linked to Santander. So I would like a little more detail about the strategy here. How do you see this strength in a scenario of evolution of Open Finance, which is one of the objectives of Banco Central, but also with this potential new social platform?
Some banks are very excited that it can help to unlock the private contract. So I would like to understand how you see the positioning of Santander here in terms of payment, and how to go to the attack and not just be defending in a scenario where the sheets may potentially lose some value in the future.
Thank you. Thank you. That was a great question.
It is true that the potentially detractors or challengers elements of a strategy to pay for the leaflet, to gain new clients, to gain principality through the leaflet, these detractors elements are growing over time, but in fact, we see Open Finance as a super positive agenda because it is also an opportunity for us. It is not necessarily made to take value from incumbent banks or Santander. In our view, and in my view, it is made to give value to Santander.
As long as we know how to approach it right and see it positively, as you said, if we have an attitude of attack and not of defense, this is the attitude that I guarantee that we are also defending. Every attacker has to defend, but we have a mentality of a net winner and not a net loser here.
So how do we do this? We do this with an offer. So the leaflet is a vehicle through which I have access to a client base. But the leaflet alone guarantees very little. It guarantees an account opening and, eventually, a salary account, because that's how it works. But I don't want the mechanical element of the leaflet, Osmar.
I want the element that allows me to actually work in the principality. So how do I actually earn through the vehicle that the leaflet allows me to do? How do I gain the principality, which is what actually changes the game and obviously brings profitability, the ROI, the bottom line that you want to follow, that we manage? With an offer. And the offer is a series of things. The summarized version of this, we can detail it later; the summarized version is that I know how to segment really well, and I know how to understand the blocks. And here we are not just talking about average income as one thing. Average income is probably 6, 8, 10 different classes.
High-income also has different classes; there is the high-income taker, I mentioned here that almost 30% of our credit portfolio, several JPFs, is a taker, and there is nothing wrong. There is a super high loss absorption, we have a hyper-profitable portfolio there, and I want to grow more in high-income credit. And there is also, of course, the high-income investor, and there is that high-income investor So, even in high-income areas, there are several classes, and in low-income areas, even more.
So, the ability to segment or sub-segment is super important, and from this sub-segmentation, going more and more into the person, and not only into the cluster, which is what I call hyper-personalization, which, yes, a lot of people have talked about it, but I would say that we are advancing a lot in completely redesigning our CRM model, completely redesigning our systems of models and credit policies. We can In practice, with the ability to sub-segment and personalize, we can understand what offer, at what moment, and on what channel, in what context, I have to offer to that client. I think that's what changes the game.
So, Folha is a big channel from which I have a large client base, and there are many millions of Folha clients that we have here, but if I do well in sub-segmentation and hyper-personalization, and I offer exactly what that client needs, in the context that he needs, with the language, and with the access, and what I call multi-channel conversation, that this client needs, then we have a chance to win the game, and that's what we're working on, and that's why the re-launching of massive income offers, for example, that's why back there we re-launched high income, that's why now I platformize my mid-income, so all the pieces in the background are connected, and it's the strategy that I've been commenting with you and other analysts for a few years, and that we're putting the pieces to run in the sequence that we get, some in parallel, and all this converging for us to actually have the real chance of having the lead, having Folha as one of the big vehicles, but not the only one. I hope I was able to answer well here. No, excellent. Thank you very much. Now we go to Thiago Batista from UBS.
Hello, Thiago. I would like to focus a little on Select. Impressive knowledge that you are showing in this segment, 1.4 million customers. You have already commented, Mario, that you have already reached 2 million customers; this will be a little above what the market leader is. This portfolio, as has been shown here, represents almost 30% of the loans and less than 5% of Anderson Select's clients. This performance is amazing.
My question here, first, is what was the most relevant change you saw in this segment to explain this improvement? And a second point here, the average ticket for this portfolio, for this segment, is more or less R$ 50,000 of credit per client. Obviously, all clients use a loan.
But the point here is, what segment are you having such a higher growth within Select? What product is leading to such a strong growth in the portfolio? Select, in this line that I just answered to Rosman, of us being able to do segmentation, I would say that the first big cluster of clients that we hugged strongly, and it was still in 2022, I commented on this the first time, in the disclosure of the third TRI, we relaunch in August, September of 2022, so a little over a year and a half ago, we relaunch Select as a whole.
We did, at that time, nine years of Select in Brazil; last year, we completed ten, and we, for the first time, did a campaign. Of course, it's not just about the campaign itself, but in the campaign, we democratize Select. What do I mean by that? We no longer accept the Select client for income or for investment.
We open Select, deep down, for anyone who wants to pay the monthly fee that we charge before the client is able to get in. And in this democratization, Thiago, we, deep down, open the doors of Select for the client who wants to have a super differentiated service. What super differentiated service is this? We also launched this back there.
It was the first segment where we, in fact, started to practice, in a very complete and precise way, the multichannel approach, which now we also want to do for this base, which is many times larger than the massive income base. So there we always had the stores, the Select stores, either individual or store-in-store, stores within stores, super cool spaces that had nothing wrong, but we left those spaces even more integrated with a personal 24x7 service.
So the Select client calls, if it wants to call, and some still want to call, it goes straight to a cell that goes straight through the URA, that is, it goes straight to a human attendant who speaks. Obviously, we also have an impeccable chatbot, but the human chatbot is also there. So the Select client realizes that it has a continuous, multichannel conversational capacity. It always has a human at its disposal, him, or her.
And besides that, we bring an element that we definitely didn't have, Thiago, which is the element for the Select client investor, which is the element of financial advice. So when we bring financial advice, which is not only the human part of AAA, but it is also a much more advanced investment portal. Until the beginning of 2021, we still owed, in a way, in terms of the digital experience of the client investor.
We have a big leap. We are about to, we are in the countdown. In weeks, we are going to launch the new version of what we call the investment portal, already much more advanced. So we bring a much more complete digital experience for the client investor. We bring human touch to the AAA, which I have already mentioned here, which has the lowest cost on the market and therefore the best ability to cover.
But along with that, this is for the client investor; we bring a multichannel, human, 24x7 offer, with stores that are there, which are super well used, and several customers love them in the stores, and several do not love them in the stores, and are well treated as well. So with that, we have an element of differentiation that we have been working on. We have also done, of course, we observe our customers from all other segments; those that we see are select customers, and by historical definition, because they were originally Van Gogh, or some were even in our low income segment, which we call special, we also bring these clients to select. So we have an element of re-characterization, yes, but it is legitimate, natural, and correct.
But in this year and a half, Thiago, to close, we have, for the first time, a very material organic growth of customers. So this number that you see growing, it has an important component of growth of organic customers who decided to be select customers, whether they came from Folha, which is, again, the answer I gave here to Osmo. We have been working better and better on Folhas and sub-segmented, more senior executives of the companies, and having them choose Santander as the main bank, and not the bank they already had, be it the traditional ones or the new ones that focus on high income. In terms of products, there is no specific product, which you also asked.
We have grown a lot, of course, in real estate. We talk little about real estate, unfairly, because we have had a relative real estate performance much better than the market. We won the quota last year; we were one of the only ones that grew. It grew a little, but it grew, and several withdrew. And in the production of these first three months of the year, we had a very powerful real estate performance.
So, between the real estate and the consigned, of course, which is also valid for high income, we have managed to differentiate several different products. There is no silver bullet, there never has been, but we have made solid growth, and that portfolio, which we expect to grow, is a reflection of that. Thank you very much, Mario. The next question now comes from Eduardo Nishio, from Genial. Hello Nishio, good morning. I think there's a connection problem.
We'll go to Yuri Fernandes from JP Morgan. Sorry, Yuri. Good morning. Good morning, Camila. Congratulations, Mario, and Gustavo, for the quarter. Mario and Pierry have already discussed a little bit about the market. I would like to go a little bit to the product margin and the client margin. We saw a good improvement in the spread here. There were some declassifications, as you have already pointed out, so our history ends up not being so long for us to look at before 2023.
So I would like your help here to understand how to think a little bit about this line. I think, from what you are saying, the impression I get is that this margin should continue to improve. I wanted to confirm that.
But how far should this margin improve? Should we go back to the beginning of 2022? I know it's not the same base, but the product margin used to be higher. Or not?
It must be something closer to what we saw at the beginning of 2023. If you could help us think about this margin, which has to do with me, which has to do with a lot of things you have commented about funding, I think it would help us not to be so loose in improving your spread. Thank you. I'll start and pass the ball to Gustavo.
Yuri, a very good question. And we, touching on the point you made about reclassifications, here we are meeting a demand. The first time I met with the analysts, at least here in Brazil, they said, ah, you have to look at Oruodo. We looked at Oruodo, so we did our first reclassification. They are correct classifications.
We didn't do it to get better or worse. We wanted to put things in the most accurate places, not that they were imprecise before, but we wanted to. So, the first move to reduce Oruodo is to meet demand from you. We hope to do another important one at the turn of next year. And if we can help, obviously, you, the analysts who study our numbers in depth, to think about the bank even before, we can do that with pleasure.
But answering precisely here, Yuri, we actually have a portfolio today, in 2024, and I would say from now on, quite different from the portfolio that entered in 2022. So, you mentioned 2022; in 2022, we had a fairly large carryover effect of the portfolio that we designed in this great growth cycle that ended in 2021. And then, at the turn of the year, which coincided with the bank's assumption, it was a coincidence; we made an important stop. You already know it well, and I don't need to repeat it.
So, in 2022, we start a redesign of the portfolio, but still with a carryover effect in the first line, and quite clear. And that's why the first line, our margin line, for six or seven consecutive quarters, constantly falls and starts to rise again to the third quarter of last year. And then there's a fourth quarter flat, and now, in fact, it starts to grow with a little more strength. How would I answer your question? Block A, the liquid margin of acquisitions. This one tends to fall, in fact, because of Selic. So, Selic will fall a little slower, so the detractor element of this line dilutes the time a little more.
But we already know this, as you all know, so we are working to compensate for this in acquisitions with volume and mix. Mix is passive, with having more of that float resource that is in the account. We have, as all banks have, the instruments of profitability to be able to have a good margin there. Obviously, we don't just want to count on floating money, so we have to bring the investor client here, then all the investment agenda, select and beyond. So, we are going to compensate for Selic's fall with volume and mix. So, we expect to have a positive performance here, even though Selic's strength is throwing this line out there.
Knowing this challenge that we have in the margin of acquisitions, we will continue to do well, and with even more strength, of course, the active part, the credit, and extended portfolio part. And here, we are actually going to look for the same type of mix that we are building here. So, you should expect an average spread level similar to the one we had back there, where the clean portfolio, the low-income portfolio, the ratings, on our scale of 1 to 10, rating 5, 6, 7, were much more present than they are today.
No, because we don't have the same mix, we don't want to have the same mix, we are working with a little on rating 8 clients and a lot on rating 9 and 10 clients. Each bank has its own scale, but you can see a dimension of where we are cutting. So, we want to have a clean exposure with 9 and 10, and even collateralized, as in the financial sector, as in the consignado, we also want to have higher ratings. So, our average rating goes up a few points, certainly, from 21 to 22.
So, we shouldn't expect, in the first line, the same level of gross spread, but obviously, we should expect the level of liquid PDD spread to improve over time because I think that's what we are showing. So, this doesn't necessarily happen in the same tree, where first you build the portfolio, you digest the portfolio, we make fewer agreements, we launch the results more, the cases that we see that we won't be able to recover in time, and Gustavo covered this a little bit, he can cover more.
So, temporarily, it's not all exactly in the same tree, but the direction of a first line of liquid credit costs, becoming more and more healthy, and obviously the digestion of the past portfolio, also flowing, this gradually creates a jawbone in this line of credit, let's call it that, that we believe we have already shown in this tree and will continue to show. So, we are positive, in summary, about how this line will behave during the year. In that case, if you go down on one side, we compensate for volume and price, and on the asset side, we will continue to grow, but with the same type of mix of products and with the same type of customer portfolio that we have sought. Gustavo, I don't know if you want to add anything. Yuri, that's exactly what it is.
So, there is no comparison between the previous portfolio and the current portfolio. In the current portfolio, we will continue with the same dynamics, so we will continue with the same ratings, we will continue with the same composition of products per client cluster, so we will continue with the same profile per microportfolio, as I said. We are advancing a lot in CP with some kind of guarantee; we had higher volumetricity with CP Clean, so we effectively change the entire composition of our portfolio. If the CDI falls, we make a composition in the passive, but also make a composition in the asset to balance it.
What we are looking for is that the liquid spread is getting bigger and bigger, and this opens up over time. This is a little of the dynamics we have. Perfect, thank you Gustavo, thank you Mario. Good luck with the results and congratulations again.
Thank you. Now we are with Eduardo Nishio from Genial. Hello Nishio, good morning. Hello Camila, good morning, everyone.
Good morning Mario, and Gustavo. Congratulations on your results. I would like to talk a little more about retail, specifically your strategy, Massificado. Congratulations on the launch. Retail has changed a lot in this cycle, and you came up with a new strategy. I would like you to talk a little more about the profitability you expect, what happened in this cycle, talk a little more about the target audience, if it is the open sea, if it is low income, your vision for Massificado and retail. Thank you. Great, Eduardo. Thank you, Unknown.
It's a good hook for us to talk a little more about massivism, so I'll try to be brief here. These are the key themes. We recognize that the client has evolved. He has evolved in the type of demand, in the type of relationship he wants to have, in the type of principality he is willing to give.
Today, the client has at least five active accounts on average and has almost four active accounts for each client. So, the way the client defines principality has changed a lot over the years, and, therefore, the ability of each digital bank, or bank, it doesn't matter; we are all digital, to work to earn, if not all the client's principality, a good part of it, also has to change a lot. So, this is super clear; we recognize the market as well.
We also recognize that the way we, and possibly the whole market, approach credit for this massive audience had to evolve. Between 2020 and 2021, the market as a whole granted credit, possibly beyond what these clients were able to absorb. Hence, the credit costs for the following years are much higher in all the banks in the market, which means that we tested, in a hard way, and learned in a hard way, the elasticity of low-income income, Eduardo.
So, what we bring from learning as a starting point for this new offer is a much finer and more precise notion of how elastic the income capacity of this audience is, which, obviously, is much less elastic than the average and high-income, and PJ itself. So, with a much better and much finer understanding of how much fits in the pocket of this low-income, and, therefore, what size of exposure we can have with each client, and what exposure is worth having with that client, which depends a lot on whether I have the transactionality of this client or not, because it's no use being the element that brings even small credit to that client, it will use my credit to pay another bank, and then I end up with an adverse selection.
So, in the end, I would say that our maturity as a management here is to better understand the context, to better understand the little elasticity that the low-income has, and to better understand the need of this client to be here at home, transacting with us, and choosing us as the principal, or in the direction of choosing us as the principal, so that we can, in fact, have a better chance in the use of that limited income to pay the So, that's the context.
It's the context that, certainly, the whole market recognizes today, so there's no great confidential information here. How do we approach this in a different way? We approach it with a starting point that is a much, much simpler offer than any offer we've ever had. An offer that is absolutely free, as we talk about in the video that you saw, free without asterisks. This is super important; it's not that we had asterisks before, but all offers, historically, incumbents and digital ones, correctly provoked, and, in a way, even criticized incumbents for this, So, we here wanted to make an offer, in fact, without conditions.
So, we act with an account and a card which is free for life, which is, in fact, free forever. And, well, where are we going to get the profitability from this? Of course, taking the client from an offer that, in addition to being free for life, brings unlimited withdrawals, which is something for those who withdraw money. This public still has the use of money for a while, and it is still relevant, so we believe that a limited withdrawal is a nice proposal.
And we also bring the element of 10 days without interest, which Santander has super strong, linked to a strong PIX key. So, the client who puts the strong PIX key here, on the cell phone or CPF, we will give them 10 days without interest, which, obviously, is a huge differentiation element.
So, adding these elements, or equalization, or differentiation, we will deliver a super simple and digital experience, with a well-integrated human conversational, and with the stores as a convenient element, as I said earlier. So, we believe that the new offer of Começa Agora, Começa Agora is the positioning as a whole, and the new offer of Free, Eduardo, will bring, deep down, a chat app in relation to what we didn't have and a positive differential in relation to what we already had, and we package it in a super simple and direct way for the client.
So, we believe that, from now on, we will bring back this client who was here but was inactive. To give you an idea, we have more or less 30 million inactive clients, our total base is 60 and a few million, and our asset base is just over 30. So, in practice, half of our clients are inactive, so there is a lot of what we are looking for here, which is to activate the inactive clients, to answer this part of your question.
And there is something, of course, about open sea capture, but it is not the open sea that we did in 2021, and possibly a good part of the market; it is the open sea, first, proportionally much smaller, much more qualified, with much more information, much more intelligence in the use of data, to understand who this differentiated client is. So, today we are much safer to look at even this open sea client, which weighs less than in the past.
But a good part here will be clients who are already in the database and who are inactive, or who are in the active database but are not so happy with the offer and are gradually leaving and giving priority to others. We want to recover these clients, reactivate the inactive ones, and, yes, make client acquisitions, but with a super-big differentiation between what we want and what we don't want. Perfect, thank you very much.
Thank you. The next question comes from Brian Flores from Citibank. Hello, Brian.
Hello Camila, and thank you very much for the opportunity to ask questions. Taking advantage of Yuri and Mario's question, which was about credit costs, how should we think about them as a percentage of the portfolio? And also, how does that connect with the renegotiation strategy, which seems to be running at lower levels now? Thank you very much.
I will start with the second part. We have already commented that we have changed the renegotiation strategy. The renegotiation dynamic remains much more selective, and the renegotiation portfolio, over time, will be reduced precisely because of the fact that we have the old portfolios being digested, as Mario mentioned.
Credit costs, at the rate that we are growing, and with the credit discipline that we have, and no change in the risk profile, it has a positive tendency to reduce credit costs. It will depend a little on how we grow and where we grow, but we have already seen a very important evolution in the last 12 months, and we may have future evolutions, but it also depends on how much we advance in the portfolios, given that we have a lot of confidence in the credit performance, and all the new portfolios that we are producing are performing exactly as we expect, so there is no surprise in relation to the new portfolios, also in relation Perfeito, obrigado.
We will now switch to English with Tito Labarta from Goldman Sachs. Good morning, Tito. Hi. Good morning, Camila.
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for the call and taking my question. Actually, a bit of a follow-up to Brian's question on the cost of risk, but more on the asset quality side. We saw, you know, the MPLs were still sort of flattish in the quarter.
I know there's maybe some seasonality in 1Q, but the SME MPLs did go up a little bit. So just how are you thinking about asset quality from here? I mean, it seems that we're past the worst of it, particularly if your provisioning levels are coming down. But at any risk to that, how do you think asset quality can evolve from here? Let me just, hi, thank you, thank you for participating. So I'm just starting off, and now I'll hand it over to Gustavo.
So the broad message, taking the opportunity for a question is, we're very comfortable with the portfolio we're building, the portfolio we've been building for the last two years, I'll say, and obviously, with the benefit of having now two-year-old vintages, one-year-old vintages, six-month-old vintages. With all that we can back test. And we continuously do that every time more and more, more precisely, and we take the small adjustment decisions much faster than we did before. So all that points to the direction that we're managing with better tools with much more modern policies and models, and the vintages are behaving well, on average. So, yes, there's seasonality, there's...
The elements that you see in the presentation relate much more to the digestion of the older vintages, which we've been embracing differently for a year already in terms of the acuerdos, the renegotiations than we did before. So Gustavo can comment better, but the direction I wanted to share with you is that, yes, we're very comfortable with the way the portfolio is behaving, the direction we're taking, and how the new vintages since 2022, by the way, are behaving. So with that, Gustavo, please. Exactly that. There are no changes.
I mentioned last quarter that potentially we'll see some volatility in the overs, but it's totally related to the old vintages and the old portfolio. So it's everything under control. So, uh, uh, in terms of the future and credit quality, is everything really under control? Okay, great.
Thanks, Mario and Gustavo. Thank you. Let's go back to Portuguese now, with Gustavo Schroden from Bradesco BBI.
Good morning, Schroden. Good morning, Cami. Thank you. Good morning, Mario, and Gustavo.
Congratulations on the results, really strong. I'd like to talk a little bit because I think we're missing a part of the equation. People have discussed the NII a lot; we talked about segmentation, product, and mix, but I'd like to talk a little bit about portfolio growth. I think it's an important component for the NII. The portfolio grew 5% year on year. I'd like to understand if there is room to accelerate this?
I think we should see this portfolio growth accelerate over the next three quarters. Do you think we can get close to 8% to 10%? Do you think it's a reasonable number for us to have here in terms of portfolio growth? And also, talk a little bit about the mix, right?
Not in the segmentation, but anyway, we saw strong growth focused on designating the vehicle. The trend is the same. And if I can get a hook here, I think portfolio growth can leverage another point, which is profitability. I'm a big fan of Roy, from 10, 11 to 14.
Do you think we can get to the end of the year with Roy closer to his recent past? Before all this deterioration that happened in the asset quality system, which made everyone hold their portfolio growth, the influence rate went up, and the impact would go up. I'd like to know if we can go back to dreaming of that Roy, closer to 18, 20.
Obviously, I understand the limitations; it's not guidance I want, but I just want to know if that's the way. Thank you. I'll start with the portfolio topic, and then I'll come to profitability. As I said, and Gustavo reinforced it later, we are growing exactly in the portfolios we want to grow. We don't have a goal here of growing the same, 10%, 100%, 8%, 12%, the same for everyone. It wouldn't be a smart way to manage the bank, and it's not what you expect from us either.
We choose the businesses in which we want to consolidate leadership or gain share, but we never want to gain share without profitability and at the cost of the credit cost of 6, 12, 18 months. You don't see us growing that way. So, we choose some businesses and detail more here in the promotional disclosure. We decided to grow here.
Cards are growing. We spoke little during a year and a half of cards because we were in a deceleration module, and we, since the third trimester, have commented more, still a little shyly. Now we're going to start talking a little more because we're starting to have the consolidation of our strategy of growing again in cards. So, I would say that when we think about the size of the growth, of course, we're not going to go all out, as you know, but we expect to grow as much as the average market is expected by Febraban. We expect, in fact, to be able to...
Given that in some businesses we know we will be able to grow more and will..., which are businesses, obviously, with a higher level of profitability, if we do it well, and I really believe that we are doing it well, we have everything to have growth here that should be equal to or greater than the market growth. In large companies, I will not tell you the same thing, because, as I said, then Gustavo reinforced, we will look for, as in everything, actually, a huge discipline of profitability.
So, where I managed to have marginal ROIs in that positive operation, and that generated economic profit above our ROIs, we, on average, if the credit risk is good, we will do it. We will look at the operation, and we will look at the cross-sell capacity on top of that operation. The attack operation, of course, has a lot of cross-sell in services, mandates, and such.
So, we will always look at the customer's vision in a way, but there will be cases where even in the customer's vision it will not make sense to do it, and we will become, as I said, a distributor and not so much a credit loader. So, here we are not in a sprint of, ah, I have to grow 8, 10, or 5, up to here in the year. We have a slight drop, but it absolutely does not worry us, because the business itself is making more money than it did in the last quarter and last year.
So, we have pretty good profitability in our attack operation on large companies. Here, it may be that we grow less than the market, but it is already ex-ante. I'm not saying it will be, but if it happens, it will be because of super-fine capital discipline, and we will compensate for this with growth, also with capital discipline, in the other operations, as we showed in the first three. So translating all this into profitability.
Well, since I will be disciplined in the attack and only do the operations that are ROE-acquitted, and since my retail operations, PF, PJ, and finance, are operations with very high profitability, of course, as long as we know how to select the right clients, and the right products, we hope that the recovery that you mentioned of ROE, which was a good recovery, will continue gradually over time. What are we looking for without guidance?
We are looking to consolidate a mid-teens, then consolidate a mid-to-high-teens, and then we will work hard to come back at some point to a very high-teens or 20s. Obviously, we are not at this level in the short term, but we are redesigning the operation, executing a very disciplined strategy, to be able to meet this. What I would like to finish is that the quality of the portfolio that is delivering this ROE, and that will deliver the ROE of the next tree, is a very different quality, much more diversified and, therefore, sustainable.
So we are less focused on the speed with which I go up the ROE 1, 2, 3 points, and yes, with the solidity that I deliver this higher ROE, to be able, from there, to seek the next leap, and so on.
Perfect, super clear, thank you and congratulations once again. Obrigado, Gustavo. I would like to thank you all for being with us this morning. After this videoconference, I and the entire team of relations with Santander investors are available to clarify any remaining questions. Thank you very much, have a great day and see you next time.
